question: What is pre advising?
answer:
Pre-advising is an important step in the academic registration process. It is a phase where students plan and select the courses they intend to take in the upcoming semester. During pre-advising, students consult with their assigned academic advisors and mentors to ensure their course selections align with their degree requirements, academic standing, and future goals.

Here are some key points about the pre-advising process at BRAC University:

Course Selection: Students can review the available courses for the upcoming semester and choose the ones they need to enroll in. This includes major courses, general education courses, and electives.

Academic Planning: Pre-advising provides an opportunity for students to plan their academic journey, ensuring they meet prerequisites and avoid scheduling conflicts.

Consultation with Advisors/Mentors: Students meet with academic advisors/mentors who provide guidance on course loads, graduation requirements, and academic performance.

System Access: Once students finalize their course plan, they can proceed to formal registration when the advising period opens. Pre-advising helps prevent delays during registration as students have already mapped out their courses.

Pre-advising is crucial for staying on track with academic goals and preventing potential issues with course availability.

question: What is main advising?
answer:
Main advising refers to the formal academic advising phase that takes place after pre-advising. In this stage, students finalize their course selections and officially register for their chosen courses. Main advising is a critical part of the registration process, ensuring that students’ course choices are reviewed and approved by their academic advisors.

Here are the key aspects of main advising:

Final Course Selection: During main advising, students confirm their course choices, often making adjustments based on availability, prerequisites, or advisor recommendations.

Advisor Approval: Academic advisors review the selected courses to ensure they align with the student’s degree plan and academic progress. Advisors also provide feedback or suggestions on course load, timing, and long-term academic planning.

Registration: After advisor approval, students proceed to register for their courses in the university’s registration system. This step locks in the student’s schedule for the semester.

Adjustments and Overrides: In some cases, students might need to make last-minute changes, such as adding or dropping courses, based on availability or changes in their academic goals. Advisors may assist with necessary overrides if a course is full or if the student needs special permission.

Follow-up: Main advising helps ensure that students are taking the correct courses to fulfill graduation requirements and stay on track academically.

Main advising is essential for ensuring that students are properly registered and that their academic plan aligns with university guidelines and personal academic goals.

question: How to get an extra seat in a particular course durning main advising?
answer:
Request the section's faculty. If he agrees then he will do the other procedures for your desired section. But you need to have a maximum of 9 credits and also if there is vacany in the other sections and the section is not clashing with the courses of the routine. Your request will be rejected. Extra Seat Request Policy [CSE]:
• The section faculty has the right to deny any extra seat request in their section.
• If a student already is in another section of the same course, the request will be denied. The student may apply for lab change when the form is circulated if they have a clash that is not solveable..
If a student doesn't have the course at all and there are other sections with empty seats, then again the request will be denied. They might be added to an available section (depending on seat availability) without any notice from our side.
• If a student has 4 courses or more then again the request will be denied.
• No extra seat for hardware courses (CSE250,CSE251, CSE260, CSE350).
• A faculty may request max 2 extra seats for a lab based course and theory based course. If the seat status is already -2 in usis, the request will be denied.
Only when there is no suitable section for the student, the student maybe granted an extra seat.

5. Take approval from the Registrar.

6. Submit the Semester Drop Form to the Registrar's Office along with the above-mentioned documents.

question: Is there any scholarship scheme for international students?

Benefits: 100% tuition and fees waiver (including semester fees, lab fees, library fees) along with food and accommodations.
Eligibility: Awarded to economically disadvantaged but meritorious students.
Requirements:
Must maintain a minimum CGPA of 3.00 on a scale of 4.00 in all semesters.

Eligibility:
Undergraduate students must complete at least 30 credits, and postgraduate students must complete at least 1/4th of their program credits.

Postgraduate students must take at least 9 credits in both the current and previous semesters.
Conditions:
Students who retake or repeat courses, or have a 'W' grade or an 'F' in any subject in the previous or current semester, are not eligible.

CGPA 3.70 - 3.84: 10% waiver
CGPA 3.85 - 3.89: 25% waiver

question: How the Club Executive Panel is created?
answer:
New Panel Selection Process

1. The club should have a student Executive Committee comprised of the President, Vice-President, General Secretary, and Financial Secretary. The Executive Committee must comprise four members. Other director positions depend on the nature of the club/forum.

Executive Committee/ Student Representatives [depends on the type of activity]. This panel will work with OCA.

1. President

2. Vice-President

3. General Secretary

4. Financial Secretary

This Director panel will be comprised of 5 to 10 positions depending on the type of activity. OCA needs the list of directors, not the transcript. 

•Director – Program

•Director - Finance

•Director - Media

•Director - Rehearsals

•Director - Logistic support

 

2. Executive Committee should be formed by conducting open elections among the members. Initially, if needed, the Executive Committee could be formed by selecting representatives from the active student members by the advisor and the OCA team.

3. Students on probation or under university disciplinary actions cannot become a member of the Executive Committee.

4. For executive committee membership, students are expected to complete 60 credits and achieve a minimum CGPA of 3.

A. Applicable for Academic Club (Co-Curricular). All four students will have a minimum CGPA of 3.

B. Applicable for Non-Academic Club (Extra Curricular). Half of the panel members (2 students) is expected to have a minimum CGPA of 3. The rest of the members (2 students) is expected to have a minimum CGPA of 2.0. This lower CGPA holder student will get the approval with a condition letter.

C. Applicable for Sports Clubs. Minimum One panel member is expected to have a minimum CGPA of 3. The other three students are expected to have a minimum CGPA of 2.0. This lower CGPA holder student will get the approval with a condition letter.

5. Every club must have one female member on the Executive Committee. Otherwise, the panel will not be approved.

6. A student cannot be a member of the Executive Committee of more than one club/forum at a time. Therefore, a student can be a member (general) of a maximum of two clubs/ forums at a time.

7. It is advised that students enrolled in the last 2 semesters of undergraduate study are not selected as new Executive Committee members of clubs and forums.

8. Every year election/selection is to be conducted for the Executive Committee in the Fall semester (September – November). The final committee must be approved by the club advisor and OCA before public announcements.

9. The president of the club must let all members know of the guidelines of the co-curricular activities.

question: How can I find out if my credits will transfer?
answer:
Courses that are similar in content with BRACU or that have equivalence with BRACU may be considered for transfer. However courses that are not directly equivalent or similar to BRACU courses may be transferred as elective courses based on approval of the credit transfer committee.
The credit transfer from other universities will not exceed 50% of the credits required for degree completion at BRAC University except Architecture.
The total credits transferred by a student from other universities should not exceed 65 credits including maximum of 21 credits in design studio courses for students of Architecture.
